description: The first READ reports a response with no two-character batch equivalent, so 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS takes its permanent-error arm, renders '9000' and the program abends with RETURN-CODE 12 before a single record is displayed. The row it seeds is what makes this case additive a second time over: it is the only row in this folder whose CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME FILLS ALL FIFTY BYTES, so the PIC X(50) span is stated at its upper boundary rather than in the wide comfort zone every fixture row sits in. THE BOUNDARY, AND WHY THE FIXTURE CANNOT EXPRESS IT: the longest trimmed CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME in app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt is NINETEEN characters - 'Hayden Pfannerstill' - measured mechanically over one-based bytes 31 to 80 of all fifty rows, with 'Stefanie Dickinson' at eighteen and "Lucious O'Connell" at seventeen behind it. Every fixture row therefore leaves AT LEAST THIRTY-ONE trailing spaces inside the field, and no fromRow and rowCount range over it can reach the width the copybook actually declares. That matters because common/FixedWidthCodec implements PIC X(n) as right-space-pad on the short side and right-truncate on the long one, and a field that never arrives full exercises neither edge: with all fifty bytes occupied there is nothing to pad and nothing to truncate, so an off-by-one in either direction has nowhere to hide - it shifts every byte after position 80. The literal is chosen so that edge is visible rather than inferred: it ENDS WITH '!' AT OFFSET 80, not with a space, and OFFSET 81 IS WHERE CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE BEGINS. A codec that padded one byte too far would push 2023-03-09 to 82 and one that truncated a byte short would pull it to 80; either way the row would no longer measure 150 and the seed-time width check would refuse it. THE DERIVATION, exactly: synthesized from app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt row 1 by replacing one-based offsets 31-80, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50), with the fifty-character literal 'ANIYA VON EMBOSSED NAME FILLS FIFTY BYTES EXACTLY!'; the other 100 bytes are unchanged - CARD-NUM 0500024453765740 at 1-16, CARD-ACCT-ID 00000000050 at 17-27, CARD-CVV-CD 747 at 28-30, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE 2023-03-09 at 81-90 carrying the copybook's own misspelling, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS Y at 91, and FILLER's fifty-nine spaces at 92-150. The literal measures exactly fifty characters and the assembled row exactly one hundred and fifty, both counted programmatically rather than by eye (practice B11). It opens with the fixture row's own name so the derivation stays traceable to its source, which is also why the HAMMING DISTANCE FROM THAT ROW IS FORTY-ONE rather than fifty: the rewritten span is fifty positions wide, but nine of them already agree - position 31, where 'Aniya' and 'ANIYA' share their capital A; position 37, where 'Von' and 'VON' share their V; and the seven inter-word spaces at 36, 40, 49, 54, 60, 66 and 72, each landing on one of the spaces the fixture row already carries there. The differences run from position 32 to position 80 inclusive and NOWHERE ELSE IN THE ROW: characters 1-30 and 81-150 are byte-identical to the fixture's first row, which is asserted mechanically rather than claimed. THE MUTATION LIVES ONLY IN THIS FILE (practice B3): app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt and its byte-identical classpath copy at src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt are read-only parity oracle and are NOT edited to add a full-width name. The inline rows member exists for exactly this need, and the row is seeded verbatim - leading zeros, the closing '!' and FILLER's trailing spaces all intact. WHERE THE BOUNDARY IS ACTUALLY ASSERTED: at seed time. ParityHarness refuses a ragged dataset, and this program's parity class requires every seeded CARDFILE row to measure CardRecord.RECORD_LENGTH, which app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy fixes at 150. A forty-nine or fifty-one character literal in the span above therefore fails the build immediately, with the failure naming the width - rather than surfacing later as a mis-decoded expiration date, which is what an unpinned boundary looks like when it finally breaks (gates G19 and G21). WHY THIS CASE DOES NOT DISPLAY THAT ROW, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO LOOK LIKE AN OVERSIGHT (practice B4): the run shape declared for case13 is an OPEN that reports '00' followed by a first READ that reports an untranslatable response, so no record is ever delivered and :78 is never reached. That shape is not this file's to choose - it is what CBACT02C's parity class declares for this slot - and FOUR sibling cases already depend on it: case09 names case13 as its counterpart on the read side and states that the ONLY difference between their fingerprints is 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' at :110 in place of 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' at :129; case17 records that the arm needs one case per rendering rather than one per status and names case13 as the untranslatable response; and case18 and case19 both count case13 among the cases that reach 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS from the READ, case19 recording that nothing else in this directory pins the permanent-error rendering at that site. A three-line normal completion here would have emitted the full-width image and read prettier, but it would have falsified four sibling case files and deleted this directory's only read-site '9000' coverage (gate G47) - a far larger loss than the display line is a gain. The boundary is therefore stated where it can be stated without disturbing any of that, in the seeded input, and the ABSENCE of a 150-character image among the expected lines is itself part of this case's assertion, exactly as it is for case12. THE RUN, once into app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:70-87 and no further. :71 displays the 38-character start banner. :72 performs 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN, whose OPEN INPUT at :120 reports '00', so :121 takes its first arm and :126-127 CONTINUE. The PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :74-81 begins its first iteration, :75 finds END-OF-FILE = 'N' and :76 performs 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT. The READ at :93 reports neither '00' nor '10', so :94 and :98 both fall through to :101 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT; :104 finds the 88-level APPL-AOK false and :107 finds APPL-EOF false, so the error arm at :110-113 runs in source order - :110 displays the 22-character 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', :111 moves the status into IO-STATUS, :112 performs 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and :113 performs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, whose :156 moves 0 into TIMING and :157 moves 999 into ABCODE before :155's 16-character 'ABENDING PROGRAM' and :158's CALL 'CEE3ABD', which does not return. Control never reaches the mainline again, so :78 never displays the seeded row, :83's 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE never runs, and :85's end banner is never written. RETURN-CODE is the 12 that :101 moved into APPL-RESULT, carried out by the abend rather than by GOBACK at :87 (gate G35), and a batch exit status carries that value to the process - which is what makes a JCL COND test on a following step behave as it does today. THE STATUS IMAGE IS DERIVED, not guessed. A response the file layer cannot express in two characters has no batch FILE STATUS to move into IO-STATUS, and the program refuses to fabricate one: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS finds its first arm true at :162-163 - IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9' - so :164 moves the '9' into IO-STATUS-04(1:1), :165-167 carry the second byte through TWO-BYTES-BINARY into IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999, where a feedback byte of binary zero renders as 000, and :168 displays the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by 9000, giving the 24-character line below. Those four N characters are source text at :168 and :172, not a placeholder for the digits that follow. It is the same paragraph and the same image case09 produces from the OPEN site, and the pairing is the point: sixteen DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' sites exist across the eight batch programs of app/cbl - two arms in each, counted rather than estimated - they all share one renderer, and one implementation is what keeps all sixteen byte-identical. REPOSITORY SEQUENCE (gate G47): startBrowse '00', then a readNext reporting a response with no two-character equivalent, then the abend. There is no readNext '10' and no endBrowse on this path, and that truncation is itself the assertion. The job is driven at tasklet and step level, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 1 read-error line + 1 status line + 1 abend line = 4 ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters. NO 150-CHARACTER IMAGE APPEARS AMONG THEM, because the READ that would have delivered the row failed instead; :96's DISPLAY inside the read paragraph is a COMMENT and no display paragraph exists, so :78 is the only live display of a record in the whole program and it is never reached. RECORD GEOMETRY, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy (01 CARD-RECORD, RECLN 150) rather than counted off a line by eye (practice B11), one-based with cumulative ends: CARD-NUM PIC X(16) at 1-16, cumulative 16, and also the RECORD KEY at :32; CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at 17-27, cumulative 27; CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03) at 28-30, cumulative 30 - which is what puts CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME at 31, since 16+11+3 = 30; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50) at 31-80, cumulative 80; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10) at 81-90, cumulative 90; CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) at 91, cumulative 91; FILLER PIC X(59) at 92-150, cumulative 150. 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150 (gate G19), and the seeded row ends in FILLER's fifty-nine significant spaces, which must not be trimmed (gate G21). The copybook declares no COMP-3, no PACKED-DECIMAL and no S9, so both numeric spans are unsigned zoned DISPLAY and there is no sign overpunch to model on a card record at all. THE MISSPELLING IS THE CONTRACT: the copybook spells the date field CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE, missing the second T, exactly as CVACT01Y spells its own ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE. It is preserved verbatim here and never corrected, because field-for-field diffing keys on the name (AAP implicit requirement I1) - and on this case it is the very field the boundary points at, which makes spelling it the source's way doubly load-bearing. WHAT THIS CASE PINS ABOUT THE UNIT: it is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C computes no balance and never opens the account file. It reads the CARD file. :29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM, FILE STATUS IS CARDFILE-STATUS; :37-40 is an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150; and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. AAP rule R1 governs - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4. A reviewer who trusts the class name will look for the wrong file and the wrong arithmetic. Nothing in this program inspects a record field at all, which is also why a fifty-byte name needs no handling: there is no trimming, no ellipsis and no 'name too long' path either to preserve or to invent (practice B5). WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C, the job declares no PARM anywhere and CBACT02C has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into, so jobParameters is empty; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset seeded, addressed solely by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150 with copybook CVACT02Y, so no dataset-name literal appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). ENCODING is US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default - and it earns the naming on this row in particular: the '!' that closes the name span is 0x21 under US-ASCII and 0x5A under IBM037, so the byte this boundary rests on is only determinate once the code page is stated (practice B8). NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty, and that emptiness is a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest - :120 opens the file INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE at all, its only output being SYSOUT at app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:27. No normalisation is declared, because this row is already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares, so neither recorded fixture-to-copybook deviation applies here. PROVENANCE: every expected value in this file is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for every offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the hundred bytes this row inherits verbatim. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution: AAP 0.7.6 proves such a run impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator alongside three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution of provenance is recorded as risk R-A (practice B12). Only the provenance changes; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diff and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand. GATES PINNED HERE: G15 (one of the twenty cases for this program), G18 (its diff count must be zero), G19 and G21 (the 150-byte width holding with the X(50) span completely full, and FILLER's fifty-nine significant spaces), G35 (the CEE3ABD site raising an abend that carries RETURN-CODE 12), G46 (binding key, never a DSNAME), G47 (the status sequence truncated at the failing read, and the permanent-error rendering at the READ site) and G51 (asserted below the HTTP and JobLauncher layers). NOT APPLICABLE: G30 and G32, since CBACT02C contains no GO TO; G33, since it declares no OCCURS; G16 and both right-pad normalisations, since carddata.txt needs neither; G20, since this program writes no record; G22 through G28, since CVACT02Y declares no V99 span and this program performs no arithmetic beyond its own status bookkeeping, so the BigDecimal and RoundingMode.DOWN gates have no subject here; and G37 through G43, since no screen is driven. One row seeded whose embossed name fills every one of its fifty bytes, none delivered, none displayed, four lines out, RETURN-CODE 12.
